subject.title: fix: add resilient fallback policy for user model overrides

question: Should explicit user session model selections remain exact by default with an operator opt-in to fallback, or should OpenClaw keep strict selection with no such policy?
rationale: This is a new persisted configuration contract that intentionally changes provider routing after a user makes an explicit model choice; code review cannot choose that product policy safely.

options.title: Sponsor strict-by-default resilient fallback
options.body: Keep existing exact-selection behavior as the default, then rebase an explicit opt-in onto current main with current-schema and provider-routing proof.

options.title: Keep user selections strictly exact
options.body: Decline the new policy surface and retain the current behavior that surfaces an error instead of substituting a configured fallback.

recommendation.title: Sponsor strict-by-default resilient fallback
recommendation.body: Keep existing exact-selection behavior as the default, then rebase an explicit opt-in onto current main with current-schema and provider-routing proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned to the open canonical report for this exact fallback behavior.
